statement: The program must provide a command-line linetype command that lists linetypes from a chosen LIN file, creates a new simple linetype (description up to 47 characters and a dash, space and dot pattern with A-type alignment) in a LIN file, and loads or sets linetypes.

acceptance.sketch: Run -LINETYPE Create, name DASHX with pattern 0.5,-0.25; the definition is appended to the chosen LIN file and can then be loaded and set current.

notes: Added from help page "-LINETYPE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide a command that opens the Linetype Manager for loading, setting and modifying linetypes, with a command-line variant offering the same operations as prompts.

acceptance.sketch: Run LINETYPE; the Linetype Manager opens, and loading a linetype from a LIN file adds it to the drawing.

notes: Added from help page "LINETYPE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide a command that sets the global linetype scale factor, defaulting to 1, regenerating the drawing so smaller factors produce more pattern repetitions per unit.

acceptance.sketch: Set LTSCALE to 0.5 on a drawing with a dashed line; the drawing regenerates and the dash pattern repeats twice as often.

notes: Added from help page "LTSCALE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide a command-line lineweight command that sets the current default lineweight (nearest valid value, with BYLAYER, BYBLOCK and DEFAULT), lists valid values, and controls lineweight units and display.

acceptance.sketch: Run -LWEIGHT and enter 0.33; the current lineweight is set to the nearest valid fixed value of 0.35 mm.

notes: Added from help page "-LWEIGHT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide a command that opens the Lineweight Settings dialog for the current lineweight, display options and units, with a command-line variant.

acceptance.sketch: Run LWEIGHT and switch units to inches; the dialog applies them and lineweights are listed in inches.

notes: Added from help page "LWEIGHT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide SETBYLAYER to change the chosen property overrides (color, linetype, lineweight, material, optionally in blocks) of selected objects to ByLayer.

acceptance.sketch: Select a red line on a blue layer, run SETBYLAYER for color, and assert the line's color is ByLayer and displays blue.

notes: Added from help page "SETBYLAYER (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide UNISOLATEOBJECTS to restore display of objects previously hidden with ISOLATEOBJECTS or HIDEOBJECTS.

acceptance.sketch: Isolate one object, run UNISOLATEOBJECTS, and assert all objects are displayed again.

notes: Added from help page "UNISOLATEOBJECTS (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must ship a standard linetype library in LIN files (metric and imperial variants, separate LT files) and load user-edited LIN files whose definitions are a name line plus an alignment-A pattern descriptor line of dash, space and dot lengths.

source.ref: About Custom Linetypes and Linetype Definitions

acceptance.sketch: Scenario: load a LIN file defining *BORDER with 'A,.5,-.25,.5,-.25,0,-.25', apply it to a line and expect a dash-dash-dot repeating pattern with those lengths.

notes: Added from help page "About Custom Linetypes and Linetype Definitions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must parse simple custom linetype definitions (two lines: name and optional description, then 'A' followed by pen-down, pen-up and dot lengths, with semicolon comments) and draw them repeating along the object, ending with a dash.

acceptance.sketch: Scenario: define *DASHDOT as 'A,.5,-.25,0,-.25', draw a line of length 2.0 and expect segments of 0.5 dash, 0.25 gap, a dot, 0.25 gap, then a final 0.5 dash.

notes: Added from help page "About Simple Custom Linetypes"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must support complex linetypes that embed text characters using the bracketed form with text string, text style and S, R, A, U, X, Y transform parameters, drawing embedded characters in full without trimming.

acceptance.sketch: Scenario: load *HOT_WATER_SUPPLY with an embedded "HW" text element using STANDARD at S=.1, draw a polyline and expect complete HW labels at the stated offsets with none clipped at vertices.

notes: Added from help page "About Text in Custom Linetypes"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must support complex linetypes that embed shapes from SHX shape files using [shape_name,shape_file,transform] with R, A, U, S, X, Y modifiers, drawn whole and never trimmed.

acceptance.sketch: Scenario: load a linetype CON1LINE referencing shape CON1 from ep.shx, draw a line and expect the shape repeated at the defined spacing, rotated as per the R/A setting.

notes: Added from help page "About Shapes in Custom Linetypes"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must give every object general properties (layer, color, linetype and its scale, lineweight, transparency, plot style) plus type-specific ones, and apply the current properties to new objects.

acceptance.sketch: Set the current layer to Dimensions and draw a line and assert it is on Dimensions; assert a circle exposes radius and area properties.

notes: Added from help page "About Object Properties"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must support transparency for selected objects or whole layers, a default for new hatches and fills, and an X-ray opacity visual style for 3D solids and surfaces.

acceptance.sketch: Set a layer transparency to 50 and assert objects on it plot at 50 percent; set an object to ByLayer and assert it inherits it.

notes: Added from help page "About Making Objects Transparent"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.
